title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00550
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center incident report documenting a UAP sighting by a commercial airline crew.
core_summary: On 28 August 2023, the crew of United Airlines flight 1560 (a Boeing 737 MAX 8) flying from San José, Costa Rica to Newark reported a large white unidentified aerial phenomenon at their 9 o'clock position while northbound at 11,500 feet, approximately 5.2 miles east-southeast of Northeast Philadelphia Airport (PNE). No evasive action was taken. New Jersey State Counter Terrorism was notified.

public_headline: United Airlines crew reported large white UAP near Philadelphia in 2023
public_tldr: This FAA incident report documents a sighting by the crew of United Airlines flight 1560 on 28 August 2023. While flying at 11,500 feet near Philadelphia, the crew reported a large white unidentified aerial phenomenon to their left; no evasive action was taken, and New Jersey counter-terrorism authorities were notified.
public_narrative:
On 28 August 2023 at 7:10 PM Eastern time, the crew of United Airlines flight 1560 — a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from San José, Costa Rica to Newark — reported seeing a large white unidentified aerial phenomenon. The object was at their 9 o'clock position, meaning to the left of the aircraft, while they were heading northbound at 11,500 feet. Their position at the time was approximately 5.2 miles east-southeast of Northeast Philadelphia Airport.

The FAA's Washington Operations Center logged the report after being advised by Washington ARTCC (Air Route Traffic Control Center), the radar facility managing that airspace. The crew did not take evasive action, suggesting they did not consider the object an immediate collision threat. New Jersey State Counter Terrorism was also notified of the sighting.

The document itself is a preliminary operational notification — essentially a log entry recording that the event happened and who was told about it. It does not contain any follow-up investigation, radar data, photographs, or analysis of what the object might have been. The only description provided is "large white unidentified aerial phenomenon," with no details on the object's behaviour, estimated size, speed, or how long it was visible.

No names of individual crew members appear in the report, and redaction levels are low — the document appears to be published largely as-is. The coordinates place the sighting over the Philadelphia–New Jersey border area.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report from one flight crew. No corroborating radar data, additional witnesses, or sensor evidence is included in this document.
The report is a preliminary notification, not a completed investigation or analysis. The FAA did not reach any conclusion about what the object was.
The only physical description of the UAP is 'large white' — no size estimate, movement pattern, or duration of observation is recorded.
No evasive action was taken, which may indicate the object was not perceived as an immediate safety threat, but could also simply reflect how the crew chose to respond.
The document does not indicate whether any further investigation was conducted after this initial report was filed.
